([[Washington, D.C.]]) * [[Greenwood Laboratory School]]
([[Springfield, Missouri]]) | college = [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = 2022-2026 | team1 = [[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years2 = 2026 | team2 = [[Club Africain (basketball)|Club Africain]] | years3 = 2026-present | team3 = [[Valmiera Glass Via (basketball)|Valmiera Glass Via]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League champion]] ([[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Mr. Show-Me Basketball]] (2021) }} '''Aminu Mohammed''' (born December 15, 2001) is a Nigerian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Valmiera Glass Via (basketball)|Valmiera Glass Via]] of the [[Latvian–Estonian Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. ==Early life== Mohammed grew up in [[Lagos]], Nigeria. At age 14, he moved to the United States to attend [[Archbishop Carroll High School (Washington, D.C.)|Archbishop Carroll High School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{cite web |last=Tachman |first=Tyler |title=Aminu Mohammed's journey and the destination he's chasing |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2020/09/21/aminu-mohammeds-journey-and-the-destination-hes-chasing/ |website=Inside the Hall |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=September 21, 2020}} In his freshman season, Mohammed earned First Team All-[[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]] honors, before transferring to [[Greenwood Laboratory School]] in [[Springfield, Missouri]].{{cite web |last=Melnick |first=Kyle |title=Georgetown Coach Patrick Ewing lands first five-star recruit in Aminu Mohammed |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/12/22/aminu-mohammed-georgetown-basketball-recruiting/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=December 22, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 34.2 points and 17.5 rebounds, leading his team to a Missouri Class 2 state title, its first state title since 1942. He was named Class 2 District 10 Player of the Year and Missouri [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |title=Greenwood Laboratory School Student-Athlete Named Gatorade® Missouri Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/54018/2019_BBB_AMohammed.pdf |publisher=[[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 15, 2019}} As a junior, Mohammed averaged 34.8 points and 15.7 rebounds per game. In his senior season, he earned [[Mr. Show-Me Basketball]], [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]], and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] honors.{{cite web |last=Wheeler |first=Wyatt D. |title=Greenwood senior Aminu Mohammed named to 2021 McDonald's All American team |url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/02/23/aminu-mohammed-georgetown-commit-named-mcdonalds-all-american/4562646001/ |website=[[Springfield News-Leader]] |access-date=April 10, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} Mohammed scored 2,709 points at Greenwood, the most in Springfield history.{{cite web |last=Lucy |first=Dan |title=Greenwood's Aminu Mohammed 2021 Mr. Show-Me Basketball |url=https://www.ozarksfirst.com/sports/greenwoods-aminu-mohammed-2021-mr-show-me-basketball/ |website=[[KOLR]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 25, 2021}} Mohammed was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]]. On December 21, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] over offers from [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] and [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]]. He became the highest-ranked player to commit to Georgetown since [[Isaac Copeland]] in 2014.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Georgetown men's basketball lands Aminu Mohammed, first five-star recruit since 2014 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30576294 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=December 21, 2020}} Mohammed was the first season-high 27 points and had 10 rebounds in an 88–77 loss to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] on February 14, 2022.{{cite news |title=O'Connell lifts Creighton past Georgetown 88-77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401400492 |access-date=February 18, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 14, 2022}} As a freshman, he averaged 13.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game. On March 31, 2022, Mohammed declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He later decided to remain in the draft. ==Professional career== On November 4, 2022, Mohammed was named to the opening-night roster for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]]{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/blue-coats-announce-opening-night-roster/n-5895485|title=Blue Coats Announce Opening Night Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} and eventually helped the team win the [[NBA G League]] title.{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Delaware Blue Coats win G League championship; Jaden Springer named Finals MVP|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/delaware-blue-coats-nba-g-league-championship-2023-jaden-springer-mac-mcclung|website=NBCSports.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] | 31 || 31 || 32.2 || .379 || .310 || .722 || 8.2 || 1.8 || 1.6 || .6 || 13.7 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Mohammed's older brother, Kabir, played college basketball for [[San Jacinto College]] before transferring to [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State]].{{cite web |last=Schiffer |first=Alex |title=Aminu Mohammed is averaging 35 points. He's about to start hearing from Missouri |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article225203675.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=January 28, 2019}} His former high school coach, Shawn Harmon, became his [[legal guardian]] in 2015 after taking in his brother two years earlier.{{cite web |last=Burton |first=Jordan |title=Nationally ranked Greenwood sophomore Aminu Mohammed has NBA dreams |url=https://www.ozarkssportszone.com/2018/10/11/nationally-ranked-greenwood-sophomore-aminu-mohammed-has-nba-dreams/ |website=Ozarks Sports Zone |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=October 11, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Wheeler |first=Wyatt D. |title=How Nigeria native Aminu Mohammed became Springfield's next basketball phenom |url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/01/02/msu-basketball-recruit-5-star-aminu-mohammed/2401024002/ |website=[[Springfield News-Leader]] |access-date=April 10, 2021 |date=January 2, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://guhoyas.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/aminu-mohammed/13262 Georgetown Hoyas bio] *{{commonscatinline}} {{Delaware Blue Coats current roster}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Mohammed, Aminu}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century Nigerian sportsmen]] [[Category:Delaware Blue Coats players]] [[Category:Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Nigerian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
